Scootch · scootch.app

Website

Play with Scootch in ten seconds, land somewhere good from every share, arrive in the app with your monster waiting, and get the serious answers plainly. Every page is shown at desktop and phone, in light and dark. The maker in section 03 is live.

System, navigation and footer

The app's inks on the web: warm paper, ink, one tomato, halftone dots, SF Pro Rounded headings. Desktop has four links and an App Store badge. On a phone the nav collapses to the logo, "Get the app" and a menu. The footer always carries helplines and the support-tool statement.

scootch.app
Every page, every timeAccessibility rules shared by all pages.
Large textEverything is in rem and reflows: one column, stacked buttons, no truncation. Tested up to 310%.
Screen readersCards are one image with the name and flavour as the label. The demo loop has a written transcript. Critters are decorative unless they are the content.
FocusA 3px tomato ring on every control, never removed.
Reduce MotionNo tilt, no flip, no idle sway. The demo becomes four stills with captions.
ContrastWhite never sits on tomato. Tomato buttons use ink text, at 5.8:1.

Home

The home page is the toy: the monster maker field is the first thing on it, and the result appears in place. Below that come a silent demo loop, three one-line ideas, a strip of real monsters, plain prices, who it's for, and the footer.

Twenty seconds, no sound

From “ugh” to caught, in four taps.

1Ramble at Scootch for twenty seconds.
2One thing comes back, and hatches.
3Start. Scootch loses its mind with joy.
4Hold to finish. The monster is yours.
ok so taxes and mum and the dentist email and the bathroom is a crime scene…Ramble at Scootch
It hatches into Molar
Start. Ten minutes.
Hold to finish. Caught.

Ramble at me. I’ll pick one thing and hide the rest in a drawer.

scootch.app/wall
Wall rules
Opt inNothing appears unless the owner taps Publish on a card in the app. One tap removes it again.
Task hiddenThe typed task line is off by default. Names and flavour are written by Scootch, never by the owner.
Checked firstAutomated check plus a person for anything flagged. Names that mention real people, health or money trouble never go up.
ReportOn every card. Two reports take a card down until it's reviewed.
No profilesNo usernames, follower counts or likes. Just monsters.

Privacy, plainly.

What gets sent, what gets kept, and what is never used to train anything. This is the same table as Settings › Privacy and data in the app.

WhatWhat’s sentHow long it’s keptUsed for training
Voice ramblesTranscribed on your phone where possible, otherwise sent encryptedAudio: never. Transcript: until the one thing is pickedNever
Typed tasksSent to write Scootch’s lines and name monstersUntil you delete themNever
Desk and Room photosNever leave your phoneOnly if you tap KeepNever
Paper and Screen photosSent encrypted to be readDeleted as soon as they’re readNever
Monster maker (web)What you type, to make the monster24 hours, unless you share the cardNever
Shared cards and recordsA public link, if you shareUntil you unshareNever
TablesA one-word label, written by ScootchWhile you’re seatedNever
AnalyticsCounts like “a session started”. No ads, no trackers, no ad IDs13 monthsNever

Export

In the app: Settings › Privacy and data › Export my data. You get one file with your tasks, monsters and records.

Delete

Settings › Privacy and data › Delete everything. It’s gone from your phone and our servers within 30 days. Deleting doesn’t cancel Plus; that’s in your Apple settings.

Questions: privacy@scootch.app. Full legal policy here, last updated 6 October 2026.

scootch.
Get the app

Terms, in human.

The legally complete version is linked at the bottom. This is what it means.

The short version

Use Scootch to start things. Don’t use it to hurt people. We’ll be straight with you about money and data.

Your stuff

Your tasks, monsters and records are yours. You give us permission to store them so the app works, and to show anything you choose to share.

Public things

If you publish to the wall or share a link, it’s public until you take it down. Don’t publish other people’s private details.

Paying

Plus is sold by Apple. Apple handles billing, refunds and cancelling. We remind you before every charge.

Not medical advice

Scootch is a support tool for starting things. It doesn’t diagnose, treat or cure ADHD or anything else. If you need care, talk to a professional.

Ending

You can delete everything at any time. We can suspend accounts that abuse tables, the wall or haunting.

Questions, answered straight.

Fifteen of them. Still stuck? help@scootch.app, and a person writes back within two working days.

Having a really hard time? Helplines
Is Scootch free?+
Do I need an account?–

No. The app works on your Apple ID. You only need an account to sit at tables, and that’s Sign in with Apple.

Is Scootch for ADHD?+
Does it diagnose or treat anything?–

No. It’s a support tool for starting things. It doesn’t diagnose, treat or cure anything, and it isn’t a substitute for care.

What Scootch is and isn't · phoneThe support-tool statement, at length.
9:41
scootch.
Get the app

What Scootch is and isn’t.

Scootch is

A small, silly companion that helps you start one thing a day, and keeps you company while you do it.

Scootch is for

People with ADHD, people who procrastinate, and anyone for whom starting is the hard part.

Scootch isn’t

A treatment, a therapist, a coach or a medical device. It doesn’t diagnose, treat or cure ADHD, depression, anxiety or anything else.

Scootch won’t

Track streaks, shame you, sell your data, or pretend a monster can replace real help.

If you need more

Talk to your doctor or a mental health professional. If you’re struggling right now, use the helplines. They’re linked from every page.

When it gets serious

If what you type sounds heavy, Scootch stops joking. No monster, no card, just a kind sentence and real people to talk to.

Press kit

Scootch is an iPhone app that helps people start one small thing a day. You ramble at a small hand-drawn critter, and it picks one task, turns it into a named monster, and sits with you while you catch it. It’s built for people with ADHD and anyone who finds starting hard. It is a support tool, not a treatment.

Motion notes

Three moving things on the site, each with its Reduce Motion form. Everything else stays still, apart from button presses.

Hatch

The hatch

Full motion
Press Hatch it0 ms
Egg wobble0–700
Crack700–1100
Card flips in1100–1700
Settle1700–1950
Buttons rise1950–2200
Reduce Motion
Press0 ms
Hatching…
“Hatching…”0–1200
Crossfade1200–1400
Done1400
EasingFlip: cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1), overshoots 6° and settles. Wobble: three damped swings.
SoundShake rattle, a crack, and the hatch chirp from the app, all in D pentatonic. Off by default on the web; it plays after the visitor's first tap.
Screen readers“Hatching” is announced, then “Hatched: Molar, Keeper of Thursday”. Focus moves to the card.

Posterstill
Play buttonon tap

TimingFour beats of five seconds each, with a 450 ms crossfade. It loops, pauses on hover or focus, and pauses off-screen.
SilentIt never plays sound. The beat captions sit next to it on desktop and under it on phones.
Accessiblearia-label carries the whole story. With Reduce Motion it doesn't autoplay: a poster frame, a play button, and the four captions.
